about: The launch view across the harbour as the game draws it beyond its kit: the rocket (the made model the game kept for it, earth_launch_rocket), the harbour, the far ground, the rocket's floodlight, the moonlight and the night sky. Frame: EarthSite's own.

objects.name: rocket
objects.from: earth_site.gd:260-262 ROCKET_AT (-270, 0, -60) and ROCKET_HEIGHT, stood on the top of the stage's launch pad pieces (1.2 m up; the game's deck lies on the ground), 1282-1285 _stand_the_rocket_up (turned PI / 2); launch_rocket.gd:14-15 TALL 60 m; the made model (data/definitions/prop.json earth_launch_rocket, a Pixal3D mesh the game kept, retired there on 2026-10-04 for the code rocket) stands in place of the code rocket at the owner's word (2026-10-09); it is 60 m tall as made, scaled by 1.0

stars.from: game/world/sky/sky.gd:19-33,517-544 (SEED 9, STAR_COUNT 1800, SKY_DISTANCE 700: a SphereMesh of radius 0.7 with 4 sides and 2 rings, scaled 0.4 to 1.3, every direction), game/art/materials/star.tres (unshaded #eef2ff); hung here at 1900 m with each star as wide seen from the middle, past everything the stage holds and inside the views' 2000 m reach, as the game hangs them just inside its camera's reach; turned with the place's own axes, where the game turns them with the world's spin and the hour, which the record does not carry

game_only: the far city across the harbour: the game hangs four photographs of Hong Kong round a ring at the sky's edge (earth_site.gd:327-335,959-972), which the scene leaves out, since no backdrop is a picture of a real place; the framework's own far city (tools/usd/far_city.py: its made towers laid as a wall along a far shore with mountains behind, drawn at night onto the same ring) waits for the owner's pick of its tower models
the lit columns the game paints onto the water (each lit thing's streak, harbour.gdshader's lit_columns); the water mirrors what stands round it
the stars' turn: the field is the game's own (its seed, count and sizes), turned with the place's axes, not with the world's spin and the hour
the ink lines over every view but the first (the page draws the game's ink pass over the first view, as a render option)
